top_strength: Patient, thorough re-probing that surfaced details the online booking missed — a 5x10 storage unit, high-rise loading-dock access, and real walking distance at the first stop — and then transparently walked the customer through exactly why the estimate moved from 4-4.5 hours to 5-5.5 hours rather than just changing the number on her silently.
coaching_note: This was a re-quote/confirmation call, but the core differentiators still apply and all three were skipped — No Worries Damage Coverage, Meet Your Mover, and the On-Time Guarantee — with the damage-coverage miss stinging most since the customer asked point-blank about wall and floor protection. Clock mechanics (2.5-hr minimum, 15-min proration) were also never explained even though hours were actively being revised. Layer these in on every call that touches pricing, not just first-touch quotes, and tighten delivery — a lot of repeated 'okay' and restarted sentences buried otherwise strong content.
phone_presence_notes: Warmth showed up in bursts ('that's perfect, perfect,' 'absolutely, my pleasure,' repeated use of the customer's name) and the customer ended clearly satisfied and thankful, but a lot of the call was mechanical detail-recitation with heavy filler/repetition rather than sustained rapport-building.
audio_review_reason: Transcript contains several garbled or out-of-context number strings (e.g. hourly rate rendered as '202', stray digit sequences like '3456' and '1234') that look like ASR errors rather than actual speech — worth an audio check to confirm the real hourly rate and clock details, since those affect the Section 3/4 scoring directly.
